info.name: ResolveAI
info.description: ResolveAI backend API. Session-cookie auth; send X-CSRFToken on unsafe requests. Every response uses the envelope {success, status_code, message, data, meta}; errors carry a stable `code`.

request.description: Sets the csrftoken cookie. The test script copies it into the csrfToken variable used by the X-CSRFToken header.

Open this URL in a browser (Postman cannot complete Google's consent screen). Redirects to Google; after sign-in the callback redirects to the frontend /app (or /login?google_error=<code>). remember=1 gives a 30-day session, otherwise 14 days. Codes: cancelled, google_failed, rate_limited, email_unverified, email_conflict, account_disabled. Add reconnect=1 to force Google's consent screen and obtain a fresh Gmail refresh token (works for signed-in users too). Sign-in now asks for Gmail send and read access; users may decline it and still log in.
Called by Google, not by clients. Listed for reference; add http://localhost:8000/api/auth/google/login/callback/ as an authorized redirect URI.
Ends the current session.
Ends every session of the user.
Own device sessions: id, device label, created_at, last_active_at, is_current. The IP is never returned.
Ends another device's session. The current session is ended with Logout (400 cannot_revoke_current_session).
Only display_name (1-80 chars); unknown fields are rejected.
Starts a 7-day grace period and ends all sessions. 409 account_owns_workspace while the user owns a workspace. Signing in again within 7 days cancels it.
slug is optional (3-40 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) and immutable. The caller becomes the owner.
Paginated (25, max 100 via ?limit=&offset=).
Owner only. slug cannot be changed.
Owner only. Hidden at once, purged after 7 days.
Owner only; target must be an active member.

size is in BYTES and must equal the real file size exactly (check the file's properties, e.g. 4392), and content_type must match what you send in the PUT; both are part of the signature, otherwise R2 answers SignatureDoesNotMatch. Returns key and a signed upload_url. PUT the raw file bytes there (Body > binary) with the Content-Type header from the response and no other auth headers, then call Confirm logo.
Owner only. The owner cannot be removed.
Members only; the owner must transfer ownership first.
Owner only. Metadata only; the token cannot be recovered.
expires_in: 1h (default), 1d or 7d. Revokes the previous link. The raw token and url are returned once.
Any signed-in user. Limited per IP (scope join_link). Invalid, expired and revoked links return the same 404.

Owner only, up to 20. Gmail addresses are matched by mailbox (dots, +tags and googlemail.com are ignored). Each result says created, already_invited or already_member. Invitations expire after 7 days. Each new invitation is also emailed to the invitee from your own Gmail (needs the Celery worker; skipped when no Gmail is connected).
Open invitations for the Google account you signed in with.
Body is Markdown/text, up to 200 KB, stored in R2 and counted in the 50 MB workspace quota. Starts as draft.
Filters: ?title=(contains) &status=draft|published|archived &category=<id> &ordering=-updated_at|title|created_at|published_at, plus limit/offset. No full-text search in v1.
Includes the content (read from storage).
Any of title, content, category_ids. Archived articles are read-only (409 article_archived).
Permanent. Frees its storage quota.
Only unlinks the category from articles.

PDF, DOCX, MD (text/markdown) or TXT, 1 byte to 10 MB (legacy .doc is refused). content_type must be application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, text/markdown or text/plain. size is in BYTES and must equal the real file size exactly. Reserves quota. Then PUT the raw bytes to upload_url (method PUT, body binary, header Content-Type exactly as returned, nothing else; create that request outside this collection), then call Confirm upload. Unconfirmed uploads are removed after 1 hour. category_id is required: the file is filed under that category.

Checks the stored object has the declared size and type (PDFs must start with %PDF-, DOCX files must be a valid zip with the Word parts). Confirming queues reading the file in the background: poll List uploads until index_status is indexed (pending, indexing, indexed or failed; index_error says why it failed). Only indexed files are searched.
Filters: category (id), filename (contains). Each item has index_status, index_error, page_count and indexed_at.
Signed URL that forces a download, valid 5 minutes.
Frees its storage quota.
used_bytes, limit_bytes (50 MB) and remaining_bytes for articles plus uploads. The logo is not counted.

Passages of published articles and ready uploaded files with citations: each result has `source` {type article|upload, id, title, page} (`article` is null for files). Words and meaning (embeddings) are both searched and merged. Up to 3 rewrites of the question are searched too; `rewritten` says whether they were used. 30 requests per minute.

Same passages (articles and uploaded files) as 'Find context for a question', plus `answered` (true when `status` is answered) and `answer`: a paraphrase written only from those passages, with [n] markers that match `results[].citation`. `status` is answered, not_covered (passages do not answer it), unavailable (LLM failed; passages still returned) or no_results. Uses up to 2 Resolve AI calls (rewrite and answer). 30 requests per minute. The exchange is saved in your chat history; add `conversation_id` to continue a chat (omit it to start a new one).
Your saved chats in this workspace, newest first. Paginated (limit, offset).
One of your chats with all its questions and answers. Another user's chat is 404.
Deletes the chat and its answers.
Your own mode, model and key summary (last 4 only) in this workspace, plus the allowed models.
Use the Resolve AI Gemini key.
Only the cheap models offered in options.resolve_ai.models.
The key is checked with the provider, stored encrypted and never returned.
Needs a saved key.

item.name: Change the model of a key (OpenAI)

request.description: Re-checks the stored key against the new model.
Forgets the key and falls back to Resolve AI mode.
Owner or member. category: billing, technical, account, feature_request, general (default), other. priority: low, medium (default), high, urgent. Gets the next per-workspace number.

body.raw:
{
  "subject": "Cannot log in",
  "description": "The customer phoned: password reset email never arrives.",
  "customer_email": "jane@example.com",
  "customer_name": "Jane",
  "category": "technical",
  "priority": "medium"
}

request.description: Filters: status, priority, category, created_from, created_to (YYYY-MM-DD), q (contains in subject, customer email and name), waiting_for_reply=true|false, assignee=<user id>|me|unassigned, ordering (number, created_at, updated_at, last_activity_at, priority, status; prefix - for descending), plus limit/offset (25, max 100).

item.name: Ticket overview (one call for the page)

request.description: Everything the ticket page needs in one request: `ticket` (detail), `viewer` (your role and permission codes), `messages` (public replies and internal notes), `events` (history), `meta` (totals and how many were returned) and `email` (your own Gmail status, for the reply box). messages_limit and events_limit (1-100, default 50) return the newest items in chronological order; older ones come from the paginated messages/ and events/ requests. Read-only; same access rules as the separate requests.
subject, description, customer_name, customer_email, category, priority. Status has its own request. On a CLOSED ticket members get 403 ticket_closed; the owner can still edit.
open, in_progress, pending, resolved, closed. Any member can change it, but only the owner can move a CLOSED ticket to another status (403 owner_only_reopen).

Assign to an ACTIVE member of the workspace (user id), 400 assignee_invalid otherwise. Owner and members may assign; on a CLOSED ticket only the owner (403 ticket_closed). Same assignee again changes nothing.
Clear the assignee.
Public messages and internal notes (agent view).
Never visible to customers.
Stored with delivery_status queued; feature 6 emails it from the agent's own Gmail. Not allowed on a CLOSED ticket.
Created, status/priority/category/details changed, reply and note added. Never contains message text.
Needs tickets.view. Summary of the public conversation only; internal notes are never sent to the LLM. Not stored. Throttle scope ai.

Needs tickets.view. `intent` is required, 1 to 200 characters. Uses the public conversation, matching published articles and the caller's name for the signature. Returns `draft` and `sources`. Nothing is sent or stored.
No login. Name, slug and logo only. 404 when the slug is unknown, the portal is switched off or the workspace was deleted.

No login, no CSRF token. Limited per IP and to 5 tickets per email address per hour per workspace. Leave the hidden field `website` empty or omit it (bots that fill it get a fake success). Returns only the ticket number.

body.raw:
{
  "customer_email": "customer@example.com",
  "customer_name": "Cara",
  "subject": "Where is my order?",
  "description": "I ordered last week and nothing arrived.",
  "category": "general"
}

request.description: Connection created by Google sign-in. status: connected, not_connected (Gmail permission declined or no refresh token), reauth_required (token expired or revoked; Testing-mode tokens last 7 days), disconnected. When reconnecting is needed `reconnect_path` is a sign-in URL that forces Google's consent screen. Tokens are never returned.

Reads at most the newest 30 inbox messages of your Gmail and files customer replies on their tickets (matched by email headers, never by subject). Mail from known customers that cannot be matched goes to the review list; everything else is ignored and not stored. Limited to 6 per minute.
Stops the push watch, revokes the grant at Google and deletes the stored refresh token. Signing in again can reconnect.
Messages from known customers that could not be matched to a ticket (sender, subject and a short snippet; newest 30, kept 30 days).
Files the message on the chosen ticket (its text is fetched from Gmail again) and removes it from the review list.
Queues a public reply whose delivery_status is failed again (sender or owner). delivery_error says why it failed: gmail_not_connected, gmail_reauth_required, gmail_rejected, gmail_unavailable.
Called by Google Pub/Sub with a signed JWT, never by clients. Listed for reference; it needs RESOLVE_AI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE and RESOLVE_AI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT.

One call for the dashboard screen. Owner and members (dashboard.view); non-members get 404. Defaults: period=30d, tz=UTC, all sections, limits 5/5/10. Cached 30 s (meta.cached). 30 requests a minute per user. Unknown query parameters return 400. Shape: backend/docs/DASHBOARD_API.md.

from and to are inclusive dates, at most 366 days, and cannot be combined with period. The previous period is the same number of days right before from. Day boundaries follow tz (IANA name; unknown names return 400).
period is 7d, 30d or 90d. include is a comma list of summary, volume, recent_tickets, waiting, activity; only those sections are returned. recent_limit, waiting_limit and activity_limit are 1 to 50.

Newest first. Owner only (members get 403, non-members 404). Filters: action (exact, e.g. ticket.status_changed), action_prefix (e.g. member., ticket., article.), actor (user id), target_type, target_id, created_from, created_to (YYYY-MM-DD), plus limit/offset (25, max 100). Read-only: no create, edit, delete or export. Each item: id, action, actor {id, name}, target {type, id}, metadata (flat facts only, never secrets, message text or email addresses), created_at. Recorded actions: workspace and member changes, ownership transfer, join links and invitations, knowledge base changes, ticket created/updated/status changed. Replies and notes are not audited (they are the ticket's own history).

exec: // Google sign-in cannot finish inside Postman. Sign in with a browser, copy the
// `sessionid` cookie value into the `sessionCookie` environment variable, and every
// request below sends it (plus the CSRF cookie when `csrfToken` is set).
